title: Responses polyfill: edge-case heuristics and runtime fallbacks
creator: Sara Leland
description:
Goal: Implement a lightweight 'polyfill' translation layer in the runtime that closes observable behavioral gaps between Redwood's Responses-compatible endpoints and the OpenAI Responses API, prioritizing correctness across streaming, tool/function calls, and structured outputs while avoiding regressions to latency or throughput.

Scope:
- Map OpenAI-style event stream tokens (delta vs final) into Redwood's existing chunking model, preserving ordering and deterministic reassembly for function-call arguments.
- Implement heuristics for handling partial/ambiguous tool calls emitted in stream (e.g., mid-token tool metadata, interleaved streaming text and tool events).
- Structured output reconciliation: validate and repair JSON/YAML fragments emitted across multiple stream frames, surface repair attempts in diagnostics.
- Behavioral fallbacks for cases where parity cannot be achieved cheaply: fallback to non-streaming re-run (single-shot) or to a compatible older model variant with different tokenization if requested.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Polyfill runs as a thin translation layer immediately after token decoding; it avoids re-tokenizing or re-running model inference where possible to keep latency impact below 5%.
- For ambiguous tool-call boundaries we prefer conservative behavior: attempt incremental reconstruction and emit a deterministic 'tool_call_reconstructed' event to Console traces; if reconstruction fails after N bytes, trigger the configured fallback policy (re-run single-shot or map to tool-missing error).
- Structured-output repair uses a streaming JSON reassembler with a small buffer cap (default 16KB). Larger messages will be escalated via an event that includes a trace_id allowing downstream replay in Dedicated/Private environments.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit + integration tests that replay 200 synthetic OpenAI-style streams covering: nested tool-calls, fragmented JSON, interleaved function args and text, and deliberate tokenization splits.
- End-to-end golden-trace comparison against a reference mapper: <confluence>/ResponsesCompatibility/PolyfillSpec and representative GH PRs linked.
- Latency P95 increase measured on CI microbenchmarks must be <= 5% when polyfill is enabled.
- Rollout switches exist: header opt-in (X-Redwood-Responses-Compat: polyfill=v1) and console toggle; telemetry emitted to track fallback triggers, reconstruction rates, and customer-visible errors.

Rollout plan:
1) Internal canary: enable for internal orgs only, run a 72h traffic test; collect metrics and golden-trace diffs.
2) Dev-customer opt-in: invite 3 integration partners to test with non-production keys.
3) Beta: default-off for new customers, opt-in toggle in Console.
4) Gradual enable by cohort with kill-switch if fallback rate exceeds threshold (>0.5% of streams).

Testing & observability:
- New meter: responses.polyfill.reconstructions (counter + labels: reason, model_variant).
- New sampler: responses.polyfill.trace_id for reconciliations that required fallbacks.
- Regression tests added to CI: responses-compat/golden_traces with automated diffing.

Open questions / risks:
- Edge cases where model emits tool-call JSON that is syntactically valid but semantically incomplete; reconstruction attempts could mis-associate arguments. Mitigation: surface reconstructed payloads in audit logs with a reconstruction score.
- Memory/CPU cost of the streaming reassembler under pathological long-running streams. Mitigation: enforce buffer caps and backpressure signal to runtime scheduler.
- Compatibility with Private deployments where telemetry is restricted. Mitigation: allow minimal-mode that emits only aggregated metrics and no trace payloads.

Artifacts:
- Spec: https://redwood.atlassian.com/ResponsesCompatibility/PolyfillSpec (internal)
- Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1209
- Test harness: gs://redwood-ci/responses-compat/golden_traces/2026-03-01/

Acceptance tests and runbooks to create if sign-off:
- Playbook: how to interpret reconstruction_score and when to disable polyfill per-customer.
- Postmortem template: include steps to re-run failed streams through the reconstruction harness.
